sentences.text: Rothia aeria is described as a Gram-positive, pleomorphic rod that forms part of the normal human oral flora and respiratory tract.
It has been characterised as a rare, facultatively aerobic Gram-positive bacillus in the Actinomycetales.
In a dense saliva time series, Rothia aeria was one of several dental plaque-specific bacteria that increased after every meal in a temporal order.
A cross-sectional study of 438 children reported that a low relative abundance of Rothia aeria in supragingival plaque was significantly associated with early childhood caries.
Case reports link it to periodontal and dental infections, and a literature review found seventeen cases of non-dental infection, of which six were in immunocompetent individuals.
